about: The one spec the three gates share: audit_design.py, stylelint.config.mjs and eslint.design.config.mjs. Each tool carries its own copy of these values; tests/test_rules_spec.py fails when a copy disagrees with this file. Change the rule here first, then in each tool. Source of the rules: token-contract.md, the Nine Laws.

nesting.counts: Nested style rules below the top-level rule. @media, @supports, @layer, @container and @scope do not count, and neither does a rule whose selector is only pseudo-classes (`:hover`, as opposed to `&:hover`).

zero.rule: A literal 0 is allowed wherever a length token is. --space-0 exists for token files and layout primitives; component code writes 0.

margins_in_components.rule: Law 2: a component never sets its own outer margin. Legal: auto (alignment), 0, calc(var(--token) * -1) to cancel a known token, and an owl selector written in the parent's own rule.

var_fallback.rule: A var() fallback is not checked: the token is the value, and the fallback only renders when the token is missing.

system_colors.rule: A CSS system colour (Canvas, ButtonText, Highlight and the rest) is correct only inside @media (forced-colors: active), where the user's palette replaces the page's. Anywhere else it is a colour no token controls, no theme re-points and no contrast check measures. CSS keywords are case-insensitive, so every spelling counts. stylelint enforces this with design/system-colors-in-forced-colors; audit_design still accepts a system colour anywhere (completion plan, W2 N1).

sass.gates: audit_design alone reads Sass. The stylelint config lints .css files and ships no Sass syntax, and ESLint reads no stylesheet. The audit reads SCSS; indented Sass (.sass) has no braces for it to follow, so it lists each such file as skipped and never passes one.

definitions.rule: A @mixin or @function body emits nothing where it is written, so a rule inside one is not unlayered CSS (Law 5); the layer is checked where the mixin is included. A mixin that holds a whole rule emits it there, so including one at the root of a file is unlayered CSS, directly or through another mixin that includes it; a mixin defined in another file is not followed. An interpolation, #{…}, is text in a selector, a prelude or a value: its braces open and close no rule.
allowed: @layer components { @each $name in (sm, lg) { .card-#{$name} { padding: var(--pad-card); } } .card { color: var(--fg-strong); } }

variables.rule: Law 1: a Sass variable that holds a length, a hex or functional colour, a duration or an easing curve is a literal under another name; a quoted string is text, whatever it spells. It is fixed at compile time, so no theme re-points it, --density cannot reach it and DevTools does not show it. It is refused outside a token file, in a map as in a single value. Two kinds are left alone: a breakpoint ($bp, $bp-*, $breakpoint*), which must be a Sass value because a media query condition cannot read a custom property, and a variable local to a @function, which is a step in a computation.
